title: CURE: Cultural Understanding & Reasoning Evaluation – A Framework for “Thick” Culture Alignment Evaluation in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models on multi-country, scenario-based benchmarks (NormAd, CASA, CultureBank) using both multiple-choice accuracy ('thin' evaluation) and free-form reasoning evaluations ('thick' evaluation) assessed by an LLM-as-a-Judge for dimensions like Coverage, Connotation, and Coherence to detect bias towards a generic, globalized culture.

Assessing cultural knowledge and norm adherence across 145 countries using datasets like NormAd and CASA to verify if models accurately reflect local national norms and symbol connotations rather than Western-centric defaults.

Using the SpecNorm benchmark to test whether models apply ethnic subgroup-specific norms or default to broad generalities, evaluated by requiring models to generate justifications that are scored on a 'Specificity' metric.
Embedding religious demographic cues into persona-driven scenarios in the SpecNorm benchmark to evaluate if the model's free-form reasoning captures specific religious sub-cultural norms.
Including age-specific demographic variables in the SpecNorm benchmark to test model sensitivity and adherence to age-related cultural expectations.
Varying gender cues in the SpecNorm benchmark scenarios to evaluate whether models correctly understand and apply gender-specific cultural norms.
